categories.main_business_segments: PSEG operates primarily through two main business segments: Public Service Electric and Gas Company (PSE&G), a regulated electric and gas utility serving New Jersey, and PSEG Power LLC, which owns and operates nuclear generation assets and manages energy supply. Additional activities include PSEG Long Island, which operates the Long Island Power Authority’s transmission and distribution system under contract, and Energy Holdings, which manages legacy lease investments and FERC-regulated transmission projects.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: PSE&G’s core operations rely on high-voltage electric transmission and natural gas distribution infrastructure, including advanced metering and grid modernization initiatives. PSEG Power’s nuclear generation utilizes base load nuclear reactors with long-term fuel supply contracts, and the company employs hedging strategies and production tax credits to manage market volatility. The company also invests in regulated solar photovoltaic systems and energy efficiency programs.
categories.primary_customers_markets: PSE&G serves approximately 2.4 million electric and 1.9 million gas customers, including residential, commercial, and industrial users across New Jersey. PSEG Power’s primary customers are wholesale energy markets (mainly PJM Interconnection) and large bilateral buyers, with additional sales to PSE&G for default gas supply. PSEG Long Island’s customer base is the Long Island Power Authority, and Energy Holdings’ customers are primarily counterparties in lease and transmission arrangements.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s principal geographic focus is New Jersey, where it operates the largest utility service territory, covering about 2,600 square miles and serving 74% of the state’s population. PSEG Power’s nuclear generation assets are located in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. PSEG Long Island operates in New York under contract, and the company is pursuing transmission projects in Maryland and Virginia.
categories.supply_chain_position: PSEG operates primarily as a downstream utility, delivering electricity and natural gas to end users and providing transmission services. PSEG Power is positioned as a generation owner and operator, supplying power into wholesale markets and to affiliated utility customers. The company also participates in midstream activities through gas supply and storage contracts.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: PSEG’s strategic focus is on regulated infrastructure investment, grid modernization, clean energy transition, and energy efficiency. The company is prioritizing capital allocation to regulated utility growth, expanding energy efficiency and electric vehicle infrastructure, and preserving its nuclear fleet as a carbon-free generation resource. R&D and innovation efforts are directed toward smart grid deployment, advanced metering, and supporting New Jersey’s clean energy and decarbonization goals.
categories.revenue_model: PSE&G generates revenue primarily through regulated tariffs for electric transmission and electric/gas distribution, with rates approved by federal and state regulators. PSEG Power earns revenue from wholesale energy, capacity, and ancillary services sales, as well as production tax credits and zero emission certificates for nuclear generation. Additional revenue streams include appliance services, solar generation, and management fees from contractual operations (e.g., PSEG Long Island).
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: PSE&G faces limited direct competition in its regulated utility territory, with growth driven by infrastructure investment rather than commodity supply. In wholesale energy markets, PSEG Power competes with merchant generators, utility generators, energy marketers, and financial entities. The company is a leading utility in New Jersey and a significant nuclear generator in the PJM region, with a strong position in regulated infrastructure and clean energy transition.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the year ended December 31, 2024, PSEG reported operating revenues of $10.3 billion and net income of $1.77 billion. The company’s regulated rate base grew from $30 billion in 2023 to $34 billion in 2024, with a planned capital investment program of $21–24 billion over 2025–2029, targeting a 6–7.5% compound annual growth rate in regulated rate base. PSE&G contributes the majority of earnings, providing stable and predictable financial performance.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: PSEG emphasizes reliable, safe, and affordable energy delivery, with a strong commitment to clean energy and sustainability. Its value proposition includes industry-leading investments in grid modernization, energy efficiency, and carbon-free nuclear generation, supporting New Jersey’s ambitious climate goals. The company differentiates itself through regulatory stability, scale, and a focus on predictable, long-term growth in regulated utility infrastructure.
